question.worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t & =-{\int }_{2}^{0}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-⟨10,\,4,\,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-10,\,-4,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying the vector addition rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{3}{2}f(t)+⟨2,\,-1,\,-2⟩\,\text{d}t & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{2}⟨2,\,-1,\,-2⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{3}{2}⟨-10,\,-4,\,2⟩+⟨2t,\,-t,\,-2t⟩{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =⟨-15,\,-6,\,3⟩+⟨4,\,-2,\,-4⟩\text{ } \\  & =⟨-11,\,-8,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
